# Addendum: FIT/Stream-Grounded Rebuild & MMP Reality Check

## 1. Rebuild estimate: FIT-grounded vs summary-only (the 7.5→5.0 reversal)

The FIT-grounded rebuild now lands at **5.0 weeks central** (IQR 3–14, n=12 full recoveries), which **agrees with the summary-only estimate**. The earlier **7.5-week** FIT figure is overturned — and plainly so.

Per `reversal_note`: 7.5 weeks came from sparse **v1** shortlist FIT coverage, where the 2012-01-07 restart mapped to 12 weeks under that thin coverage. With richer v2 streams and a proper proxy ladder (FIT MMP-20 → 20-min max → NP → avg → EF → speed/HR), that restart and others resolve faster. This is **not** summary optimism — it's better data. Treat **~5 weeks** as your working rebuild constant after a typical 6–8 week off-season layoff, while respecting the long tail: several rebuilds ran 10–19 weeks (2011-11-20: 12; 2013-11-01: 19; 2012-11-13: 14), and three plateaued lower rather than recovering (2009-09, 2010-04, 2016-03).

## 2. True MMP year curves vs stated historical peaks

All year curves below are **MEASURED_MMP** (wall-clock 1 Hz; zeros/gaps>8s→0; spikes>1800W rejected):

| Year | MMP-20 | MMP-60 | Coverage note |
|------|--------|--------|---------------|
| 2012 | 281.7 | **267.1** | solid (22 rides) |
| 2013 | 302.3 | 296.3 | solid (21 rides) |
| 2014 | 273.8 | 258.6 | ok (10 rides) |
| 2015 | 303.7 | 271.5 | solid (26 rides) |

**Overturned:** any earlier "2012 MMP-60 ≈159W / low fitness" reading is wrong. The measured 2012 year peak is **267.1W MMP-60 (MEASURED_MMP)** — genuine ~60-min climbing fitness.

Reconciling the stated peaks (no contradictions here):
- 2012 Alps Day 4 "~253W 60-min" is **MEASURED_MMP**; the year peak **267.1W (MEASURED_MMP)** is a different (Day 1) effort. Both real, no conflict.
- 2012 "FTP ~242W" is a **DEVICE_SETTING** — not a measurement, not a contradiction against the 267W MMP.
- 2016 Jan "FTP 260W" is a **DEVICE_SETTING** (stale config) — ignore as a fitness datum; measured 2016 MMP-60 was **172.5W (MEASURED_MMP)**.
- 2015 "critical power 282W" is **MODELLED / lore**; measured 2015 MMP-5 was **329.9W (MEASURED_MMP)**. No conflict — different constructs.

Method caveats: flat 20:60 ratios (e.g. 2013 ratio_20_60 = 1.02) can reflect a genuine **steady plateau ride** (same effort holds power out to 60 min), **not a bug**. Plausibility flags on 2010/2011/2013/2016 mostly reflect sparse/short-duration coverage, not necessarily bad data.

## 3. Path to 3.5 W/kg — coupled weight + power only

Current: **220W FTP (DEVICE_SETTING)**, 92 kg → **2.39 W/kg**. Note your best measured 20-min power (2015: **303.7W MMP-20, MEASURED_MMP**) already implies far more than 220W of ceiling — a fresh MMP-20 test should reset the baseline before chasing the ratio.

To reach 3.5 W/kg you need **~322W at 92 kg**, or less if weight also drops. But weight is **not** a free lever — dropping weight tends to cost some watts. Bands below show W/kg if you drop to the target weight while losing **0 / 3 / 6 W per kg**, starting from an assumed **~300W** current sustainable power (MEASURED_MMP-anchored, not the 220 device setting):

| Weight | 0 W/kg lost (unrealistic) | 3 W/kg lost | 6 W/kg lost |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| 92 kg | 300W → 3.26 | 300W → 3.26 | 300W → 3.26 |
| 88 kg | 300W → 3.41 | 288W → 3.27 | 276W → 3.14 |
| 84 kg | 300W → 3.57 | 276W → 3.29 | 252W → 3.00 |
| 80 kg | 300W → 3.75 | 264W → 3.30 | 228W → 2.85 |

Read this honestly: **the 0-W column is a fantasy** — do not plan around it. At 3 W/kg lost, weight loss barely moves the ratio; at 6 W/kg lost, it goes *backward*. **Power must lead.**

**Sequence:**
1. **Consistency first** — string together uninterrupted training. Your own rebuild data (~5 weeks) says a clean block restores fitness fast; the plateau cases (2009/2010/2016) are what happen without it.
2. **Retest MMP-20** to set a real power baseline (the 220 device figure understates you).
3. **Modest deficit under the training** — small enough that MMP-20 holds or rises.
4. **MMP-20 guardrail:** if 20-min power falls while weight falls, **the deficit is too aggressive** — back off the deficit, protect the watts.

Target the ratio through **power gain first, weight second**, tracking both.

# Endurance Rebuild Analysis — 2009–2016 Garmin History

## 1. Rebuild-Rate Verdict

**Central estimate: ~5 weeks to recover after a layoff (FIT-grounded, agrees with summary).**

Across 15 major layoffs (≥6 weeks), you fully recovered in **12 of 15 cases**, with a median of ~5 weeks and an IQR of **3–14 weeks**. The FIT-grounded rebuild estimate (`rebuild_fit`) also lands at 5.0 weeks, so this is not a proxy artefact.

**You are a fast responder** — but with a caveat. The distribution is bimodal:
- **Fast rebuilds (3 weeks):** repeated cleanly — 2012, 2013, 2014 (×2). When your baseline was modest and you restarted with volume, you snapped back inside a month.
- **Slow rebuilds (10–26 weeks):** the 16-week 2010 layoff took **26 weeks** to recover; the 11.6-week 2013→2014 winter took **19 weeks**. Longer layoffs cost you disproportionately longer rebuilds.
- **3 plateaued-lower events** (2009, 2010, 2016) where you never got back to prior baseline before the next gap.

**Bottom line:** you rebuild quickly *from short interruptions*, but long layoffs (>10 weeks) trigger a much slower, sometimes incomplete return. Your history rewards not-stopping far more than it rewards clever training.

---

## 2. Path Back Toward 3.5 W/kg (from 2.39 W/kg @ 220 W, 92 kg)

Current: **220 W / 92 kg = 2.39 W/kg** (this 220 W is best read as a working figure; see §5 on device settings).

Target 3.5 W/kg is a large gap. Two coupled levers — watts up, kg down — but **weight is not a free lever**: dropping kg tends to drag some watts with it. Here is the W/kg band under 0 / 3 / 6 W lost per kg, for a **6 kg** drop (92 → 86 kg):

| W lost per kg | Watts at 86 kg | W/kg |
|---|---|---|
| 0 W/kg (best case) | 220 | **2.56** |
| 3 W/kg (moderate) | 202 | **2.35** |
| 6 W/kg (worst case) | 184 | **2.14** |

**Weight alone can move you backwards.** At 6 W/kg lost, a 6 kg drop *lowers* your W/kg. Weight loss only helps if watts are held or rising through training.

Now hold weight and raise watts — to hit 3.5 W/kg you need roughly:
- At 92 kg: **322 W** (near your MEASURED 2013 MMP-60 of 296 W — a genuine stretch).
- At 86 kg: **301 W** (close to your 2012/2015 measured 60-min ceiling).

So the realistic route is **watts first, modest deficit second**:

**Sequence:**
1. **Training consistency first.** Your own data says uninterrupted riding is the dominant driver. Build a streak — your longest ever was just 8 weeks (2012). That is the single biggest untapped lever.
2. **Modest deficit under consistent training** — small enough that you don't bleed watts (aim toward the 0–3 W/kg-lost end, not aggressive cuts). Let weight come off slowly *while* power holds.
3. **MMP-20 as guardrail.** Track your 20-minute measured MMP as the objective check that watts are holding/rising as weight drops. If MMP-20 falls while you're dieting, you're in the 6 W/kg-lost regime — back off the deficit.

**Realistic timeframe:** 3.5 W/kg is not a 5-week rebuild — it's a build to a level you last touched (in power terms) in 2012–2013 at lower body mass. Expect **months of consistency**, not weeks. The 4.0 stretch is above anything in your measured history.

---

## 3. What the Consistency / Gaps Pattern Says

This is the core story. **29 gaps ≥21 days** and **12 layoffs ≥6 weeks** across 7 years. You have never trained in a genuinely structured, continuous way — every peak was built on "on/off" cycling and then abandoned.

- **Seasonal collapse is your signature.** Almost every autumn/winter shows a 6–12 week layoff (Nov 2009, Nov 2010, Oct 2011, Nov 2012, Nov 2013, Nov 2014). You rebuild each spring from scratch.
- **Volume is declining and erratic:** 170.9 h (2009) → 65.7 h (2014) → 49.2 h cycling (2016). The engine had less to work with in later years.
- **Longest unbroken streak: 8 weeks.** You have literally never sustained the kind of block that compounds fitness.

The implication is blunt: **your ceiling has always been capped by interruption, not by talent or trainability.** A fast responder who keeps stopping never banks the gains. If you want 3.5 W/kg, the intervention is boringly simple — remove the layoffs.

---

## 4. Peak Blocks / Accidental Consistency

Your best training blocks were **accidental, not planned** (all flagged `accidental_consistency: true`):

- **2009 dominates the top blocks** — three of the top five are summer 2009 (up to 59.4 h in ~9 weeks, 2.5–3.7 rides/week, ~140 min median duration). This was your highest-volume era, before power meters.
- **2012-07-17 → 08-27** (54.7 h, 3.2 rides/week) is the only non-2009 block in the top five — and it directly precedes your strongest measured power year.

The pattern: when you accidentally strung together 6–8 weeks of ~140-minute rides at 2.5–3.5×/week, fitness followed. **You don't need novel training — you need to reproduce these blocks on purpose and not stop.**

---

| Year | MMP-20 (W) | MMP-60 (W) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2012 | 281.7 | **267.1** | strong |
| 2013 | 302.3 | **296.3** | **best measured** |
| 2014 | 273.8 | 258.6 | lower volume |
| 2015 | 303.7 | 271.5 | strong 20-min |
| 2016 | 213.9 | 172.5 | detrained |

**Your measured aerobic ceiling was 2013 (~296 W for 60 min, ~302 W for 20 min).** That is the honest high-water mark to benchmark against.
